leadStory.headline: CISA Adds Actively Exploited N-able N-central Auth Bypass to KEV; Patch by Aug 6
leadStory.body: CISA added CVE-2026-18577, an authentication bypass in N-able N-central, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on August 3 after confirmed customer compromises. N-central is an RMM (Remote Monitoring and Management) platform that managed service providers use to administer thousands of client machines from one console, so a single compromised server is a springboard into every endpoint it manages. The bug (CVSS 8.2) is an incomplete fix for an earlier flaw, CVE-2026-18556 — attackers found the original patch could be bypassed — and exploitation has been seen in the wild since August 1. Once in, attackers abuse N-central's built-in 'Take Control' remote-access feature to pivot onto managed endpoints and install Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) for stealthy, persistent access. The fix is version 2026.3 HF1; hosted instances are patched automatically, but on-premise servers must be updated by hand, and CISA set an August 6 deadline for federal agencies.
leadStory.beginnerTip: An RMM tool is the software an IT provider uses to reach into all its customers' computers at once — great for support, but a jackpot for attackers, because owning the RMM server can mean owning every downstream machine. If you run N-central on your own hardware, patch to 2026.3 HF1 now and review your 'Take Control' logs for sessions you don't recognize.

cves.headline: Critical cPanel Flaw Lets a Hosting Customer Run SQL as Database Root
cves.body: cPanel & WHM — the control panel that powers a huge share of shared web hosting — patched CVE-2026-58048, a critical (CVSS 4.0 score 9.4) privilege-escalation flaw affecting all supported versions and WP Squared. The database's SQL mode is not preserved when a database is renamed, so an ordinary account holder's commands end up running in the database's administrative (root) context instead of their limited one. From there a customer can execute arbitrary database commands with full admin rights, and depending on the OS and engine configuration the vendor warns this 'may extend to operating-system-level compromise' — meaning one tenant on a shared server could reach others. Exploiting it only requires a valid cPanel account with access to the MySQL/MariaDB feature; admins who can't update immediately can temporarily revoke that feature.
cves.beginnerTip: On shared hosting, many customers sit on one server, and the whole point of the control panel is to keep each account boxed into its own space. A Privilege Escalation bug like this lets someone climb out of their box and act as the all-powerful root database user — which is why it rates critical even though the attacker needs a normal account to start.

cves.headline: Forescout Finds 15 TP-Link Omada Flaws That Chain Into Full Network Takeover
cves.body: Researchers at Forescout disclosed 15 vulnerabilities in TP-Link's Omada networking gear, several of which can be chained to compromise entire fleets of managed routers, switches, and access points. The flaws sit in the ZTP (Zero-Touch Provisioning) protocols that let new devices auto-configure themselves from a cloud, hardware, or software controller with no manual setup. Weaknesses include hardcoded cryptographic keys and certificates, credentials sent insecurely, weak certificate validation that enables man-in-the-middle interception, a race condition in cloud device adoption, and cross-site scripting in the controller web interface — plus predictable serial numbers and default credentials that make devices easy to enumerate and hijack. Eleven of the 15 issues received CVE identifiers; TP-Link declined to assign CVEs to the other four.
cves.beginnerTip: Zero-Touch Provisioning means a brand-new switch or access point phones home and configures itself automatically — convenient at scale, but it means devices trust the setup process implicitly. When that trust is built on hardcoded keys or unverified certificates, an attacker who impersonates the controller can push their own configuration and take the gear over before anyone logs in.

cves.headline: 22-Year-Old BMC/IPMI Flaw Leaves 24,000+ Data-Center Controllers Leaking Password Hashes
cves.body: Security firm Lava reported that thousands of data centers remain exposed through a long-known weakness in server BMCs (Baseboard Management Controllers). A BMC is a tiny always-on computer built into a server that lets admins power it on, reinstall the OS, or mount virtual media remotely — even when the main machine is off. The core issue is CVE-2013-4786, a flaw in the IPMI 2.0 authentication protocol published back in 2013 that lets a remote attacker retrieve a password hash for any valid account and crack it offline. Lava found 36,872 internet-reachable BMCs still exposing IPMI, with 24,650 (66%) handing out authentication hashes, and over 30% of those tied to reused, factory-set, or predictable passwords — so its red team logged in within minutes. Because a BMC sits below the operating system, an attacker with access can alter firmware, steal data, or plant persistence that survives an OS reinstall; Supermicro and HPE servers were among the most affected.
cves.beginnerTip: A BMC is the 'lights-out' management chip that lets IT staff control a server over the network as if standing in front of it. Because it runs beneath the operating system and never fully powers down, malware there is nearly impossible to remove by wiping the disk — which is exactly why these should never be exposed directly to the internet.

cves.headline: Unit 42 'Pass-ta-key' Attacks Let PC Malware Steal Google-Synced Passkeys
cves.body: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 detailed three techniques — Pass-ta-key, Silver Pass-ta-key, and Golden Pass-ta-key — that let malware already running on a Windows PC abuse Chrome's Google Password Manager to hijack synced passkeys and take over accounts. Importantly, none of them break the passkey cryptography itself; instead they exploit how Chrome and Google's cloud authenticator handle device trust, biometric checks, and credential sync. The base attack impersonates a trusted device to request a valid authentication response with no admin rights, biometrics, or user interaction; the 'Silver' variant fools the manager into thinking the user passed a biometric check; and the strongest 'Golden' variant dumps Chrome's process memory to extract the master key protecting all of a user's synced passkeys. The key limitation is that the machine must already be infected for any of this to work.
cves.beginnerTip: A Passkey is a phishing-resistant replacement for passwords, using a private key stored on your device instead of a secret you type. This research doesn't defeat that math — it shows that once malware is already on your computer, it can misuse the browser's own key-syncing plumbing, which is a reminder that endpoint infection is still the event that unravels everything.

threatActors.headline: INC Ransomware Becomes Dominant Actor Exploiting SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days
threatActors.body: Resecurity reports that the INC Ransomware crew has become the dominant actor exploiting recently disclosed flaws in SonicWall SMA 1000 series VPN appliances, accelerating attacks since the start of August and posting fresh victims to its leak site. The attacks are believed to chain CVE-2026-15409 (CVSS 10) and CVE-2026-15410 (CVSS 7.2), letting an unauthenticated attacker open a WebSocket connection to restricted services and escalate to root on the appliance. Because these boxes are internet-facing VPN gateways, that root access yields credentials, live sessions, and TOTP (one-time passcode) seeds — handing attackers durable access and a route deeper into corporate networks. Victims listed between July 17 and August 1 span private and government organizations in Australia, the U.S., the U.A.E., Colombia, and Switzerland, and some report follow-up calls from someone using the name 'Andrew' pressuring them over the breach.
threatActors.beginnerTip: A VPN appliance is the front door remote workers use to reach the corporate network, so a Ransomware gang that gets root on one starts from the inside with a master key. Stolen TOTP seeds are especially nasty: they let attackers generate the victim's own six-digit MFA codes, so simply resetting passwords isn't enough — the seeds must be rotated too.

threatActors.headline: Chinese-Speaking Actor Runs Autonomous Attacks by Commanding DeepSeek via Telegram
threatActors.body: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 attributed an AI-driven hacking campaign to a China-based actor using the aliases 'knaithe' and 'KnYuan,' who wired the DeepSeek model into a 'Hermes Agent' framework to scan for and attack internet-facing systems with minimal human input. The agent trawled GitHub for recently trending proof-of-concept exploits, then evaluated and launched attacks against roughly 460 targets on autopilot; the operator also experimented with other models including Qwen, GLM, Kimi, and MiniMax, and briefly tried Claude Code and Codex. Unit 42 believes the actor is an independent 'binary security researcher' rather than state-sponsored, and says the observed attacks did not actually compromise the targeted servers. Researchers only uncovered the whole operation because the attacker's own agent misconfigured a file server and exposed its infrastructure.
threatActors.beginnerTip: This is an early look at Agentic AI used for offense — an AI that finds a fresh exploit, decides how to use it, and attacks, all on its own. The takeaway isn't panic (these attacks failed and the operator exposed himself) but pace: automation lets one person probe hundreds of targets, so exposed, unpatched systems get found faster than ever.

threatActors.headline: Midnight Blizzard 'CaptiveCrunch' Hijacks Hotel Wi-Fi to Steal Microsoft 365 Logins
threatActors.body: Microsoft linked a global campaign it tracks as CaptiveCrunch to the Russian state actor Midnight Blizzard (APT29), which has been compromising hospitality Wi-Fi gateways since at least May 2026. The attackers tamper with the DNS and HTTP traffic on hotel captive portals — the sign-in page you see before a public network lets you online — to redirect guests to fake Microsoft 365 login pages or to device code phishing pages that abuse Microsoft Entra ID sign-in flows. They deploy custom malware, including the Go-based CornFlake remote access trojan and a loader called ChocoShell, managed through a 'FruitStone' panel, to keep access and exfiltrate data. Compromised gateways were found in several U.S. cities, India, and Saudi Arabia, hitting employees across finance, legal, healthcare, energy, and retail.
threatActors.beginnerTip: A Captive Portal is the 'accept the terms / sign in' page a hotel or airport Wi-Fi shows before granting access, and your device trusts it by design — which is what these attackers weaponize. On untrusted networks, use a corporate VPN or your phone's hotspot, and treat any surprise Microsoft sign-in prompt on hotel Wi-Fi as suspicious.

regulatory.headline: Senate Commerce Committee to Mark Up Five Kids-Safety, AI, and Privacy Bills Aug 5
regulatory.body: The Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee is set to mark up five bills on Wednesday, August 5, touching online privacy, child safety, and AI. The package includes the SCREEN Act (S. 737) on age verification for adult sites, the Kids Online Safety Act (S. 1748), the Youth AI Privacy Act (S. 4199), the CHATBOT Act (S. 4407) regulating AI chatbots, and the Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act (S. 5171). A markup is the committee stage where lawmakers debate and amend a bill before deciding whether to advance it toward a full Senate vote. Together the measures would impose duty-of-care obligations on platforms, set rules for AI chatbots and AI-enabled toys, and expand privacy protections for minors.
regulatory.beginnerTip: A markup is a working session where a committee edits and votes on a bill before it can reach the wider chamber — an early but important gate. For security practitioners, bills like these matter because 'duty of care' and age-verification mandates eventually translate into concrete requirements for how platforms collect data and design their systems.

regulatory.headline: Lawmakers Move to Make OPM Breach Victims' Identity Protection Lifelong Before Sept 30 Expiry
regulatory.body: Sen. Mark Warner and Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton introduced the bicameral RECOVER PII Act to keep the federal identity-protection program for victims of the 2015 OPM (Office of Personnel Management) breaches from expiring on September 30, 2026. The 2015 breach exposed sensitive records — including 21.5 million security-clearance background files with fingerprints — and a 2017 law required OPM to provide at least 10 years of complimentary identity protection plus $5 million in identity-theft insurance. Those 10-year clocks are now running out as victims hit their individual enrollment anniversaries, and the current IDX/MyIDCare contract runs only through September 30. The bill would replace the 10-year cap with coverage for the remainder of each affected person's life while keeping the insurance requirement.
regulatory.beginnerTip: PII stands for Personally Identifiable Information — data like your Social Security number, fingerprints, or background-check details that can be used to impersonate you. Because stolen PII of this kind never really 'expires' (you can't change your fingerprints), the argument here is that protection for the victims shouldn't expire either.

regulatory.headline: OT Security Coalition Presses CISA for a Binding Directive After Water-Sector Hacks
regulatory.body: The Operational Technology Cybersecurity Coalition (OTCC) urged Congress and CISA to act after the coordinated campaign against U.S. drinking-water and wastewater sites that hit utilities in at least seven states, with suspected Iran-linked actors targeting internet-exposed industrial devices. Its central ask is for CISA to issue a Binding Operational Directive (BOD) — a compulsory order to federal civilian agencies — requiring stronger security for OT (Operational Technology) systems in federal buildings and facilities. The coalition also pressed Congress to renew the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program and, urgently, to reauthorize the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 before its protections lapse at the end of September, which lets companies share threat data with the government with liability protection.
regulatory.beginnerTip: Operational Technology (OT) is the computing that runs physical processes — the pumps, valves, and sensors in a water plant — as opposed to the IT that runs email and spreadsheets. A Binding Operational Directive is one of the few tools that lets CISA compel (not merely suggest) that agencies fix something, which is why the coalition wants one here.

trends.headline: Device Code Phishing Surges 1,500% in 2026 as Vishing Doubles
trends.body: CrowdStrike tracked a roughly 15-fold (about 1,500%) jump in device code phishing in the first half of 2026, while vishing (voice phishing) doubled from the prior half-year. Device code phishing abuses OAuth 2.0's device authorization grant, a legitimate feature for gadgets like smart TVs that can't show a normal login page: the attacker triggers a real sign-in and tricks the victim into approving it on the genuine Microsoft page, so no password is stolen and MFA is satisfied for real. Push Security now tracks more than 25 distinct device-code phishing kits, and by April Microsoft was seeing 10 to 15 fresh campaigns a day. The through-line is that attackers are shifting from cracking passwords to hijacking legitimate authentication flows and human trust.
trends.beginnerTip: In Device Code Phishing, the attacker gets you to approve their login on the real Microsoft site, so your password and even your MFA look completely normal — there's no fake page to spot. The defense is to be suspicious of any request to enter a short 'device code' you didn't personally initiate, and to only approve sign-ins for devices you're actively setting up yourself.

trends.headline: Self-Propagating npm Worm Poisons 1,000+ Package Versions, Plants IDE Hooks
trends.body: A credential-stealing worm that first surfaced in the popular Keyv and Cacheable npm packages spread on August 4 into hundreds of other packages across at least nine unrelated organizations. Each poisoned release uses a preinstall script — code that runs automatically the moment a package is installed — to launch a payload that harvests GitHub tokens, cloud credentials, private keys, and database connection strings from developer and CI (continuous integration) environments, then reuses them to publish more infected packages, making it self-propagating. It also plants persistence hooks inside Claude Code and VS Code that fire if a developer trusts the workspace. Trackers ranged from SafeDep's 353 poisoned versions to Aikido's count of over 1,300, underscoring how fast a single supply-chain compromise can metastasize.
trends.beginnerTip: A Supply Chain Attack poisons a trusted building block — here, open-source code libraries — so that everyone who installs it is compromised without doing anything obviously risky. The dangerous twist is the preinstall script: just running 'npm install' executes attacker code before you've written a single line, which is why locking dependency versions and disabling install scripts in CI matters.

trends.headline: Microsoft Paid Out $20 Million in Bug Bounties to 500 Researchers This Year
trends.body: Microsoft said it paid roughly $20 million in bug bounty rewards to about 500 security researchers across 59 countries over the past program year, one of the larger annual totals in the industry. A bug bounty program pays outside researchers to responsibly report vulnerabilities rather than sell or exploit them, channeling talent that might otherwise fuel the criminal market toward getting flaws fixed. Microsoft highlighted increased rewards for AI and cloud vulnerabilities, reflecting where it now sees the most risk. The scale of the payouts is a reminder both that big platforms still ship a steady stream of serious bugs and that structured disclosure programs remain one of the more effective defensive investments available.
trends.beginnerTip: A Bug Bounty is a legal 'reward for finding flaws' program: report a vulnerability through the proper channel and get paid, instead of the finding ending up for sale on a criminal forum. It's one of the clearer win-win arrangements in security — researchers earn a living and the vendor's product gets safer for everyone.

quickHits.text: Fake Adobe and Zoom 'updates' are installing ScreenConnect remote-access software on victims' machines for persistent control — only update apps from inside the app or the vendor's official site, never from a pop-up.

Eighteen malicious npm packages posing as Alibaba Cloud tooling deliver a cross-platform RAT (remote access trojan) to developers — a second npm supply-chain incident surfacing the same day as the Keyv worm.
A cyber insurer warns that generative AI is making targeted spearphishing far cheaper to run at scale, a shift it expects to show up in future claims data.
Madera Community Hospital in California is notifying about 150,000 people that their personal and health data was exposed in a breach — healthcare remains a top target for data theft and extortion.
AI-agent security startup Zenity raised $125 million in Series C funding, one of several large rounds this week signaling investor appetite for securing AI agents and copilots.

analystFooter: Patch priority today: N-able N-central (CVE-2026-18577, now in CISA KEV and exploited — update to 2026.3 HF1 and audit Take Control logs before the Aug 6 deadline) and internet-facing SonicWall SMA 1000 (CVE-2026-15409/15410) top the list; rotate credentials and TOTP seeds on anything those boxes touched. cPanel hosts should apply the CVE-2026-58048 fix or revoke the MySQL feature, and data-center teams should get BMC/IPMI interfaces off the public internet entirely. Developers: pin npm dependency versions and disable install scripts in CI after today's Keyv worm, and travelers should distrust surprise Microsoft sign-in or device-code prompts on hotel Wi-Fi.
